question: At every frame phase near each committed Night 7 binding's declared epoch, does the seed or the phase decide the night, and what would identifying the seed add to a controller choosing among those bindings?
answer: Over 1000 held-out seeds at 121 frame phases (+-1000 ms) per binding, 481 of 484 (binding, phase) cells are decided by the phase alone (every seed wins or every seed loses). Knowing the seed and choosing among the 4 bindings beats the best single binding at 0 of 121 phases, by at most 0 seeds. campaign-night7-k2 and campaign-night7-k3 (both declared at 2433 ms) differ at 1 phase(s) (frames 8). campaign-night7-i's effective interval [2487, 2522] ms is not fully won; campaign-night7-j's effective interval [2417, 2452] ms lies inside a fully won band; campaign-night7-k2's effective interval [2410, 2445] ms lies inside a fully won band; campaign-night7-k3's effective interval [2410, 2445] ms lies inside a fully won band.
whyItIsModelOnly: No device run. The exact lane with the whole schedule moved by whole frames; the phone delivers a phase the anchor aims but does not measure, and per-press lateness is not in this lane.

seeds.definition: the first 1000 seeds, ascending, outside the design block (winner-census.mjs designBlock)

phases.relativeTo: each binding's anchorEpochMs + phaseOffsetMs; map index i is frame i - window

method.family: the night's committed phase-aware winner-v1 bindings; the oracle picks among them per seed
method.win: sim.won AND splitAt >= 0, as night7-presets.mjs and minus-toys-plan.mjs --gate score it
